messages.subject_clean: Combine Linear measurements and landmarks coordinates for GDF creation.
messages.body_plain:
Hello all ! :)

In my project I have some 16 landmarks, 4 linear measurements (Fin lengths), for 435 fish.

1) I regressed the procrustes coordinates of the landmarks against PC1 of my first PCA to get rid of the "bending" effect (when fish bend after dying that usually shows up in PC1). From that I got residuals that I kept.
2) I regressed my linear measurements against the length of the fish to remove size effects. I kept the residuals.

Now I want to create a gdf that would have all the data together (Residuals of Linear measurements + landmarks), along with some information (lake of origin, age of fish etc). I want to use that gdf to do some linear models to test for homogeneity of allometric trajectories, that type of stuff.

The problem is that I fail to combine the residuals of the landmarks with the residuals of the linear measurements and get an output that looks like the output of a gpagen object and that can be called in one variable in a model.
For example:
Model_wanted <- procD.lm(f1 = Shape  ~ Length + Lake, data = Combined_gdf)
AND NOT
Model_Unwanted <- procD.lm(f1 = Linear1 + Linear2 + Landmark1 + Landmark2 ... + LandmarkXXX  ~ Length + Lake, data = Combined_gdf)

And I can't do a gpagen on the data combined because my landmarks are bidimensional and my linear measurements are unidimensional so they won't combine that way.

Would someone have some ideas of script to do that, please?
I can provide screenshots or scripts if my problem is unclear!

Many thanks!!
Cheers
Noé

messages.body_plain:
Noé

Procrustes superimposition is only appropriate for landmarks and semilandmarks, not other types of morphological data like linear measurements. Thus, the pipeline would be to perform GPA first, before combining data.

I should also mention that combining data, while seemingly useful to obtain more information on the phenotype, is not as simple as it sounds. Concatenating columns of landmark-based shape variables with linear measurements will certainly result in nonsensical outcomes. The reason is that they are variables of incommensurate units and scale; thus, distances and directions and covariances among objects in that dataspace have no biological or statistical meaning (see Adams and Collyer 2019 Ann. Rev. Ecol. Evol. Syst. for discussion). That will also affect the linear models you were trying to implement; they too will have little interpretive meaning.

If one wishes to combine such data for downstream analyses, one path forward is to combine standard normal deviates of all traits. These are at least in common units/scale across variables. But of course, the original variation (and thus covariation) will be lost.

Dean

messages.subject: Unwanted landmark mirroring after GPA
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am doing a 3D analysis of symmetry in dolphin skulls using landVR.
To do this, I need to create a new shape array where half of the skull landmarks (single points only) are mirrored to the otehr half of the skull, to be comprared with the real data I manually placed on both halves of the skulls.

The mirrored dataset construted with the "mirrorfill" function in paleomorph looks ok, but after GPA in geomorph the landmark order in the aligned coordinates has changed, with the two halves beign flipped (waht wa son the left was on the right and vice versa).
This of course makes using landVR impossible. The GPA fucntion in Morpho (procSym) doesn't have this problem.
Is there a setting I can change to avoid this?

I attach some code and pictures to demonstrate the problem.
Thank you, best wishes
Agnese

#Mirror left on right
shape_array_LM_mirror <- mirrorfill(A = mirror_array,  l1 = as.integer(midline), l2 = bilat.landmarks) # the NA rows are now filled so that the numbers are the same on both

#Plot mirrored landmarks
mirror_plot <- c(#left red
                 spheres3d(shape_array_LM_mirror[landpairs_L,,23], col = mypalette_paired[6], radius = 1.5),
                 #right blue
                 spheres3d(shape_array_LM_mirror[landpairs_R,,23], col = mypalette_paired[2], radius = 1.5),
                 #midline dark gray
                 spheres3d(shape_array_LM_mirror[midline,,23], col = "gray10", radius = 1.5))

#GPA mirrored landmarks
#Geomorph - problem reflection landmarks
gpa_mirror <- gpagen(shape_array_LM_mirror)

#Check LMs
mirror_plot_gpa <- c(#left red
                     spheres3d(gpa_mirror$coords [landpairs_L,,23], col = mypalette_paired[6], radius = 0.003),
                     #right blue
                     spheres3d(gpa_mirror$coords[landpairs_R,,23], col = mypalette_paired[2], radius = 0.003),
                     #midline dark gray
                     spheres3d(coords_mirror[midline,,23], col = "gray10", radius = 0.003))

#Morpho - ok
gpa_mirror_morpho <- procSym(shape_array_LM_mirror)

#Check LMs
mirror_plot_gpa_morpho <- c(#left red
  spheres3d(gpa_mirror_morpho$rotated[landpairs_L,,23], col = mypalette_paired[6], radius = 0.003),
  #right blue
  spheres3d(gpa_mirror_morpho$rotated[landpairs_R,,23], col = mypalette_paired[2], radius = 0.003),
  #midline dark gray
  spheres3d(gpa_mirror_morpho$rotated[midline,,23], col = "gray10", radius = 0.003))

messages.body_plain:
Agnese,

It’s a good bet that this is the arbitrary flipping of PC axes, as you aligned configurations to principal axes (PCs) in both the geomorph and Morpho cases, by choosing the default options.  (Small procedural note: Morpho uses the PCs of the first specimen; geomorph uses the PCs of the reference [mean] configuration.)

You can tell by the black points that the vertical axis (PC 2) is flipped rather than left becoming right and right becoming left.

This eigen-analysis artifact poses no consequence for your data.  If it is aesthetically troubling, you can use (geomorph) rotate.coords to flip the axes as you like.

Mike

messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

Similar to the post here <https://groups.google.com/g/geomorph-r-package/c/1ZFjnOtj8N8/m/GKzI2DZ_BQAJ>, I am trying to calculate the confidence intervals for a set of Zcr values derived from the ‘compare.Cr’ function. I have looked into the code provided <https://datadryad.org/stash/dataset/doi:10.5061/dryad.h18931zfs> and found that these were calculated using the following code where res.spec and res.hypoth are the results from two iterations of the compare.Cr function (one comparing different species and different modularity hypotheses respectively):

#Species

CI.sp<-qnorm(res.spec$sample.r.sd <http://sample.r.sd>)/2

#Hypotheses

CI.h<-qnorm(res.hypoth$sample.r.sd <http://sample.r.sd>)/2; CI.h[1] <- 0

I am wondering if someone would be able to walk me through this calculation- is it based on a specific formula for calculating confidence intervals? More specifically, I am a little lost on what the qnorm function is doing in this context, but would appreciate any general explanation on what this calculation is doing.

Thanks in advance for any help!

Rossy
